items.title: 🎯 What is a Data Structure?
items.text: Definition: A data structure is a scheme of organizing data in the memory of the computer in such a way that various operations can be performed efficiently on this data.
path: Unit 1: Introduction to Data Structures & C Fundamentals

items.title: Why Do We Need Data Structures?
items.text:
1. Large amounts of data - Computers deal with text, images, relational data, etc.
  2. Data is raw material - For information, analytics, business intelligence, advertising
  3. Organization matters - The way data is organized in memory plays a key role in deciding time complexity of algorithms
  4. Data Structures & Algorithms go hand in hand - You can't have efficient algorithms without proper data structures

items.title: 🧠 Abstract Data Type (ADT)
items.text:
ADT is used to represent data and operations associated with an entity from the point of view of user irrespective of implementation.

  • ADT specifies WHAT operations are supported, not HOW they are implemented
  • Same ADT can be implemented using different data structures
  • Example: Stack ADT can be implemented using Array OR Linked List

items.title: Static Memory Allocation
items.text:
• Allocated by compiler at compile time
  • Exact size and type must be known at compile time
  • Memory allocated in stack area
  • Examples: int b; int c[10];

Disadvantages: - Size cannot be altered at runtime - May lead to under/over utilization of memory - Memory cannot be deleted explicitly - Only useful when data size is fixed and known beforehand

  • Functions defined in <stdlib.h>

items.title: malloc()
items.text:
void *malloc(size_t size);
- Takes number of bytes to allocate - Use sizeof to determine size of a type - Returns void* (can be assigned to any pointer) - Returns NULL if no memory available

Example: Allocate space for 100 integers

if ((p = (int*)malloc(100 * sizeof(int))) == NULL) {
    printf("out of memory\n");
    exit(1);
}

items.title: calloc()
items.text:
void *calloc(size_t nitem, size_t size);
- Allocates memory and initializes to zero - Requires two arguments: number of items and size of each item

Example: 

int *p = (int*)calloc(100, sizeof(int)); // 100 ints, all zeros

items.title: realloc()
items.text:
void *realloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size);
- Resizes previously allocated block - Two arguments: pointer to existing block, new size

Example: 

int *ip = (int*)malloc(100 * sizeof(int));
// ... later need twice as much ...
ip = (int*)realloc(ip, 200 * sizeof(int));

items.title: free()
items.text:
void free(void *ptr);
- Deallocates memory allocated by malloc/calloc/realloc - Takes a pointer as argument

Critical Concepts: - Dangling Pointer: Pointer to memory that has been freed - Memory Leak: Allocated memory with no pointer to it (cannot be freed)

// DANGEROUS - Dangling pointer
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
free(p);
// p now dangles - points to freed memory!
// *p = 10; // UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR!

// DANGEROUS - Memory leak
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
*p = 30;
p = malloc(sizeof(int)); // First block lost forever!

items.text: A linked list is a linear data structure where: - Elements (nodes) are NOT stored in contiguous memory - Each node contains data and a pointer (link) to the next node - Head/start pointer points to the first node - Last node's link contains NULL

items.title: Insertion Operations (3 Cases)
path: Unit 1: Introduction to Data Structures & C Fundamentals

items.title: Case 1: Insert at Beginning
items.text:
void insert_front(NODE **head, int value) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    temp->data = value;
    temp->link = NULL;

    if (*head == NULL) {
        // Empty list - new node becomes head
        *head = temp;
    } else {
        // List not empty - insert before current head
        temp->link = *head;
        *head = temp;
    }
}

Visual Walkthrough: 

Before: head → [10|•] → [20|•] → [30|NULL]

Insert 5 at front:
1. Create node with data=5, link=NULL
2. temp->link = head (points to 10)
3. head = temp (points to 5)

After:  head → [5|•] → [10|•] → [20|•] → [30|NULL]

items.title: Case 2: Insert at End
items.text:
void insert_end(NODE **head, int value) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    temp->data = value;
    temp->link = NULL;

    if (*head == NULL) {
        *head = temp;
    } else {
        NODE *curr = *head;
        // Traverse to last node
        while (curr->link != NULL) {
            curr = curr->link;
        }
        // curr is now last node
        curr->link = temp;
    }
}

items.title: Case 3: Insert at Given Position
items.text:
void insert_at_pos(NODE **head, int value, int pos) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    temp->data = value;
    temp->link = NULL;

    if (*head == NULL || pos == 1) {
        // Empty list or insert at front
        temp->link = *head;
        *head = temp;
        return;
    }

    NODE *curr = *head;
    NODE *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;

    // Traverse to position
    while (curr != NULL && i < pos) {
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->link;
        i++;
    }

    if (curr == NULL) {
        // Position beyond end - insert at end
        prev->link = temp;
    } else {
        // Insert between prev and curr
        prev->link = temp;
        temp->link = curr;
    }
}

items.title: Case 2: Delete Last Node
items.text:
void delete_end(NODE **head) {
    if (*head == NULL) {
        printf("List empty\n");
        return;
    }

    if ((*head)->link == NULL) {
        // Only one node
        free(*head);
        *head = NULL;
        return;
    }

    NODE *curr = *head;
    NODE *prev = NULL;

    // Traverse to last node, keeping track of previous
    while (curr->link != NULL) {
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->link;
    }

    // curr is last node, prev is second-last
    prev->link = NULL;
    free(curr);
}

items.title: Case 3: Delete at Given Position
items.text:
void delete_at_pos(NODE **head, int pos) {
    if (*head == NULL) {
        printf("List empty\n");
        return;
    }

    if (pos == 1) {
        // Delete first node
        NODE *temp = *head;
        *head = (*head)->link;
        free(temp);
        return;
    }

    NODE *curr = *head;
    NODE *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;

    while (curr != NULL && i < pos) {
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->link;
        i++;
    }

    if (curr == NULL) {
        printf("Invalid position\n");
        return;
    }

    if (curr->link == NULL) {
        // Last node
        prev->link = NULL;
    } else {
        // Middle node
        prev->link = curr->link;
    }

    free(curr);
}

void delete_node_dll(dll_t *list, NODE *temp) {
    if (temp == NULL) return;

    if (temp == list->head && temp == list->tail) {
        // Only node
        list->head = list->tail = NULL;
    } else if (temp == list->head) {
        // First node
        list->head = temp->next;
        list->head->prev = NULL;
    } else if (temp == list->tail) {
        // Last node
        list->tail = temp->prev;
        list->tail->next = NULL;
    } else {
        // Middle node
        temp->prev->next = temp->next;
        temp->next->prev = temp->prev;
    }

    free(temp);
}

items.title: Josephus Problem (Classic Application)
items.text:
Problem: n people in circle, eliminate every k-th person, find survivor.

int josephus(int n, int k) {
    // Create circular list 1..n
    node_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        temp->key = i;
        if (!head) head = tail = temp;
        else { tail->next = temp; tail = temp; }
    }
    tail->next = head;  // Make circular

    node_t *curr = head, *prev = tail;
    while (curr->next != curr) {
        // Count k-1 steps
        for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) {
            prev = curr;
            curr = curr->next;
        }
        // Eliminate curr
        prev->next = curr->next;
        free(curr);
        curr = prev->next;
    }
    int survivor = curr->key;
    free(curr);
    return survivor;
}

items.text:
// sll_complete.c - Complete Singly Linked List Implementation
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *next;
} NODE;

NODE *create_node(int data) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    if (!temp) { printf("Memory full\n"); exit(1); }
    temp->data = data;
    temp->next = NULL;
    return temp;
}

void insert_front(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    temp->next = *head;
    *head = temp;
}

void insert_end(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    if (*head == NULL) { *head = temp; return; }
    NODE *curr = *head;
    while (curr->next) curr = curr->next;
    curr->next = temp;
}

void insert_at_pos(NODE **head, int data, int pos) {
    if (pos <= 1 || *head == NULL) { insert_front(head, data); return; }
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;
    while (curr && i < pos) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; i++; }
    if (!curr) { prev->next = temp; }
    else { prev->next = temp; temp->next = curr; }
}

void delete_front(NODE **head) {
    if (!*head) return;
    NODE *temp = *head;
    *head = (*head)->next;
    free(temp);
}

void delete_end(NODE **head) {
    if (!*head) return;
    if (!(*head)->next) { free(*head); *head = NULL; return; }
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    while (curr->next) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; }
    prev->next = NULL;
    free(curr);
}

void delete_at_pos(NODE **head, int pos) {
    if (!*head) return;
    if (pos <= 1) { delete_front(head); return; }
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;
    while (curr && i < pos) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; i++; }
    if (!curr) { printf("Invalid position\n"); return; }
    prev->next = curr->next;
    free(curr);
}

void display(NODE *head) {
    printf("List: ");
    while (head) { printf("%d → ", head->data); head = head->next; }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

int main() {
    NODE *head = NULL;

    printf("=== Singly Linked List Demo ===\n");
    insert_end(&head, 10);
    insert_end(&head, 20);
    insert_end(&head, 30);
    display(head);  // 10 → 20 → 30

    insert_front(&head, 5);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 20 → 30

    insert_at_pos(&head, 15, 3);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 15 → 20 → 30

    delete_front(&head);
    display(head);  // 10 → 15 → 20 → 30

    delete_end(&head);
    display(head);  // 10 → 15 → 20

    delete_at_pos(&head, 2);
    display(head);  // 10 → 20

    return 0;
}

// memory_demo.c - Dynamic Memory Allocation Demo
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int main() {
    printf("=== Dynamic Memory Demo ===\n\n");

    // 1. malloc
    printf("1. malloc():\n");
    int *p = (int*)malloc(5 * sizeof(int));
    if (!p) { printf("Failed\n"); return 1; }
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) p[i] = (i+1)*10;
    printf("Allocated 5 ints: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) printf("%d ", p[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(p);
    p = NULL;  // Good practice: set to NULL after free

    // 2. calloc (zero-initialized)
    printf("\n2. calloc():\n");
    int *q = (int*)calloc(5, sizeof(int));
    printf("Zero-initialized: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) printf("%d ", q[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(q);

    // 3. realloc
    printf("\n3. realloc():\n");
    int *r = (int*)malloc(3 * sizeof(int));
    r[0] = 1; r[1] = 2; r[2] = 3;
    printf("Before realloc: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) printf("%d ", r[i]);
    r = (int*)realloc(r, 6 * sizeof(int));
    r[3] = 4; r[4] = 5; r[5] = 6;
    printf("\nAfter realloc:  ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) printf("%d ", r[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(r);

    // 4. Structure allocation
    printf("\n4. Structure allocation:\n");
    struct student {
        char name[20];
        int roll;
        float marks;
    };
    struct student *s = (struct student*)malloc(sizeof(struct student));
    strcpy(s->name, "Alice");
    s->roll = 101;
    s->marks = 95.5;
    printf("Student: %s, Roll: %d, Marks: %.1f\n", s->name, s->roll, s->marks);
    free(s);

    printf("\n=== Dangling Pointer Demo ===\n");
    int *dang = (int*)malloc(sizeof(int));
    *dang = 100;
    printf("Before free: *dang = %d\n", *dang);
    free(dang);
    // dang is now DANGLING - don't use it!
    dang = NULL;  // Always set to NULL after free

    printf("\n=== Memory Leak Demo ===\n");
    // BAD: memory leak
    // int *leak = malloc(sizeof(int));
    // leak = malloc(sizeof(int));  // First block lost!

    // GOOD: free before reassign
    int *good = malloc(sizeof(int));
    *good = 42;
    free(good);
    good = malloc(sizeof(int));
    *good = 84;
    free(good);
    printf("No leaks!\n");

    return 0;
}

// circular_josephus.c - Circular List & Josephus Problem
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int key;
    struct node *next;
} node_t;

node_t* create_node(int key) {
    node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    temp->key = key;
    temp->next = NULL;
    return temp;
}

void insert_clist(node_t **head, int key) {
    node_t *temp = create_node(key);
    if (*head == NULL) {
        temp->next = temp;
        *head = temp;
    } else {
        temp->next = (*head)->next;
        (*head)->next = temp;
    }
}

void disp_clist(node_t *head) {
    if (!head) { printf("Empty\n"); return; }
    node_t *temp = head;
    printf("Circular: ");
    do {
        printf("%d ", temp->key);
        temp = temp->next;
    } while (temp != head);
    printf("\n");
}

// Josephus Problem
int josephus(int n, int k) {
    node_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        temp->key = i; temp->next = NULL;
        if (!head) head = tail = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        else { tail->next = temp; tail = temp; }
    }
    tail->next = head;  // Make circular

    node_t *curr = head, *prev = head;
    // Find tail (node before head)
    while (prev->next != head) prev = prev->next;

    while (curr->next != curr) {
        for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) {
            prev = curr;
            curr = curr->next;
        }
        prev->next = curr->next;
        free(curr);
        curr = prev->next;
    }
    int survivor = curr->key;
    free(curr);
    return survivor;
}

int main() {
    printf("=== Circular List Demo ===\n");
    node_t *head = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) insert_clist(&head, i*10);
    printf("List: "); disp_clist(head);

    printf("\n=== Josephus Problem ===\n");
    printf("n=7, k=3: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(7, 3));  // 4
    printf("n=5, k=2: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(5, 2));  // 3
    printf("n=41, k=3: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(41, 3)); // Historical: 31

    return 0;
}

items.title: What is a Stack?
items.text: Stack is a linear data structure that follows LIFO (Last In First Out) principle. - Insertion: Push (at top) - Deletion: Pop (from top) - View top: Peek/Top

items.title: Real-World Analogy
items.text:
• Stack of plates in a cafeteria
  • Stack of books on a desk
  • Browser back button (history stack)
  • Function call stack (recursion)

}

}

items.title: Application 1: Parentheses Matching
items.text:
Problem: Check if parentheses in expression are balanced.

Algorithm: 

For each character in string:
    If '(', '[', '{' → push to stack
    If ')', ']', '}' → 
        If stack empty → NOT balanced
        Pop and check if matching pair
After loop: if stack empty → balanced, else NOT balanced

Matching Pairs: - ( matches ) - [ matches ] - { matches }

int is_balanced(char *expr) {
    stack_t s; init_stack(&s);

    for (int i = 0; expr[i]; i++) {
        char ch = expr[i];
        if (ch == '(' || ch == '[' || ch == '{')
            push(&s, ch);
        else if (ch == ')' || ch == ']' || ch == '}') {
            if (is_empty(&s)) return 0;
            char top = pop(&s);
            if ((ch == ')' && top != '(') ||
                (ch == ']' && top != '[') ||
                (ch == '}' && top != '{'))
                return 0;
        }
    }
    return is_empty(&s);
}

Example Traces: 

Input: "({[]})"     → BALANCED
Stack: ( → { → [ → pop[ matches ] → pop{ matches } → pop( matches ) → empty ✓

Input: "({[)]}"     → NOT BALANCED
Stack: ( → { → [ → pop[ but got ) → MISMATCH ✗

items.title: Application 2: Infix to Postfix Conversion
items.text:
Definitions: - Infix: Operator between operands (A + B) - Postfix: Operator after operands (A B +) - Prefix: Operator before operands (+ A B)

Why Postfix? No parentheses needed, easy to evaluate with stack!

Precedence Table: | Operator | Precedence | |----------|------------| | ^ | 3 (highest)| | * / % | 2 | | + - | 1 |

Algorithm (Shunting Yard): 

For each token in infix:
    If operand → output
    If '(' → push to stack
    If ')' → pop and output until '('
    If operator:
        While stack not empty AND 
              precedence(top) >= precedence(current) AND top != '(':
            pop and output
        push current operator
After loop: pop remaining operators to output


int precedence(char op) {
    if (op == '^') return 3;
    if (op == '*' || op == '/' || op == '%') return 2;
    if (op == '+' || op == '-') return 1;
    return 0;
}

void infix_to_postfix(char *infix, char *postfix) {
    stack_t s; init_stack(&s);
    int j = 0;

    for (int i = 0; infix[i]; i++) {
        char ch = infix[i];

        if (isalnum(ch)) {
            postfix[j++] = ch;  // Operand goes to output
        } else if (ch == '(') {
            push(&s, ch);
        } else if (ch == ')') {
            while (!is_empty(&s) && peek(&s) != '(')
                postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
            pop(&s);  // Remove '('
        } else {  // Operator
            while (!is_empty(&s) && precedence(peek(&s)) >= precedence(ch))
                postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
            push(&s, ch);
        }
    }
    while (!is_empty(&s)) postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
    postfix[j] = '\0';
}

Trace Example: 

Infix:  A + B * C
Step 1: A          → output: A
Step 2: +          → push +
Step 3: B          → output: AB
Step 4: *          → push * (higher precedence than +)
Step 5: C          → output: ABC
End:   pop * → output: ABC*  pop + → output: ABC*+

Postfix: ABC*+

items.title: Application 3: Postfix Expression Evaluation
items.text:
Algorithm: 

For each token in postfix:
    If operand → push to stack
    If operator:
        pop operand2 (right)
        pop operand1 (left)
        result = operand1 operator operand2
        push result
Final result = pop stack


int evaluate_postfix(char *postfix) {
    stack_t s; init_stack(&s);

    for (int i = 0; postfix[i]; i++) {
        char ch = postfix[i];
        if (isdigit(ch)) {
            push(&s, ch - '0');  // Convert char to int
        } else {
            int b = pop(&s);  // Right operand
            int a = pop(&s);  // Left operand
            int result;
            switch(ch) {
                case '+': result = a + b; break;
                case '-': result = a - b; break;
                case '*': result = a * b; break;
                case '/': result = a / b; break;
            }
            push(&s, result);
        }
    }
    return pop(&s);
}

Trace Example: 

Postfix:  3 4 + 5 *
Step 1: 3 → push 3      Stack: [3]
Step 2: 4 → push 4      Stack: [3, 4]
Step 3: + → pop 4, pop 3 → 3+4=7 → push 7   Stack: [7]
Step 4: 5 → push 5      Stack: [7, 5]
Step 5: * → pop 5, pop 7 → 7*5=35 → push 35  Stack: [35]
Result: 35

items.title: What is a Queue?
items.text: Queue is a linear data structure following FIFO (First In First Out). - Insert at rear (enqueue) - Remove from front (dequeue)

items.title: Real-World Examples
items.text:
• Printer queue
  • CPU process scheduling
  • Ticket counter line
  • Breadth-First Search (BFS)

items.title: Structure
items.text:
struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *next;
};
typedef struct node node_t;

struct queue {
    node_t *front;  // First element
    node_t *rear;   // Last element
};
typedef struct queue queue_t;

items.title: Enqueue (Insert at Rear)
items.text:
void enqueue(queue_t *q, int val) {
    node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    temp->data = val;
    temp->next = NULL;

    if (q->rear == NULL) {
        // Empty queue - new node is both front and rear
        q->front = q->rear = temp;
    } else {
        q->rear->next = temp;
        q->rear = temp;
    }
}

items.title: Dequeue (Remove from Front)
items.text:
int dequeue(queue_t *q) {
    if (q->front == NULL) return -1;  // Empty

    node_t *temp = q->front;
    int val = temp->data;

    q->front = temp->next;
    if (q->front == NULL)  // Was last element
        q->rear = NULL;

    free(temp);
    return val;
}

items.title: Why Circular Array?
items.text:
• Array is fixed size
  • Simple indices: front=0, rear=0 initially
  • Use modulo arithmetic to wrap around
  • Waste ONE slot to distinguish full vs empty

items.title: Structure
items.text:
#define MAXSIZE 5

struct queue {
    int data[MAXSIZE];
    int front;  // Index of front element
    int rear;   // Index of rear element
};
typedef struct queue queue_t;

items.title: Key Concept: Modulo Arithmetic
items.text:
Index = (Index + 1) % MAXSIZE

Visual: 

Array size 5: [ ][ ][ ][ ][ ]
                ↑
              front=rear=0 (empty)

Enqueue 10:  rear = (0+1)%5 = 1, data[1]=10
    [ ][10][ ][ ][ ]
           ↑   ↑
          f=0  r=1

Enqueue 20:  rear = (1+1)%5 = 2, data[2]=20
    [ ][10][20][ ][ ]
           ↑     ↑
          f=0   r=2

... continue until r=4
    [50][10][20][30][40]
     ↑            ↑
    f=0          r=4

Enqueue 50: rear = (4+1)%5 = 0
    rear == front? → FULL! (wasted one slot)

items.title: Operations
items.text:
void init_queue(queue_t *q) {
    q->front = q->rear = 0;
}

int is_empty(queue_t *q) {
    return q->front == q->rear;
}

int is_full(queue_t *q) {
    return (q->rear + 1) % MAXSIZE == q->front;
}

void enqueue(queue_t *q, int val) {
    if (is_full(q)) { printf("Queue full\n"); return; }
    q->rear = (q->rear + 1) % MAXSIZE;
    q->data[q->rear] = val;
}

int dequeue(queue_t *q) {
    if (is_empty(q)) return -1;
    q->front = (q->front + 1) % MAXSIZE;
    return q->data[q->front];
}

items.title: What is a Priority Queue?
items.text: Priority Queue is a queue where each element has a priority. - Dequeue removes highest priority element (not FIFO) - Higher numeric value = higher priority (typically)

items.title: Real-World Examples
items.text:
• Hospital ER: Critical patients first
  • CPU scheduling: Real-time processes first
  • Network packets: QoS priority
  • Dijkstra's algorithm

};

items.text: Implementation Enqueue Dequeue Space Unordered List O(1) - add at rear O(n) - search max O(n) Ordered List O(n) - find position O(1) - remove front O(n) Unordered Array O(1) - add at end O(n) - search + shift O(n) Ordered Array O(n) - find + shift O(1) - remove end O(n) Heap (Tree) O(log n) O(log n) O(n)

items.title: Implementation 1: Unordered Linked List
items.text:
Enqueue: O(1) - Add at rear Dequeue: O(n) - Traverse to find max priority

job_t dequeue(pqueue_t *q) {
    // Find max priority node
    node_t *max_prev = NULL, *max_curr = q->front;
    node_t *prev = NULL, *curr = q->front;
    int max_pri = curr->job.priority;

    while (curr) {
        if (curr->job.priority > max_pri) {
            max_pri = curr->job.priority;
            max_prev = prev;
            max_curr = curr;
        }
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->next;
    }

    // Remove max_curr
    job_t job = max_curr->job;
    if (max_prev == NULL)  // Was first node
        q->front = max_curr->next;
    else
        max_prev->next = max_curr->next;

    free(max_curr);
    return job;
}

items.title: Implementation 2: Ordered Linked List
items.text:
Enqueue: O(n) - Find correct position by priority Dequeue: O(1) - Remove from front

void enqueue(pqueue_t *q, job_t *job) {
    node_t *temp = create_node(job);

    // Insert in descending priority order
    if (!q->front || q->front->job.priority <= job->priority) {
        // Insert at front
        temp->next = q->front;
        q->front = temp;
        if (!q->rear) q->rear = temp;
    } else {
        // Find position
        node_t *curr = q->front;
        while (curr->next && curr->next->job.priority > job->priority)
            curr = curr->next;
        temp->next = curr->next;
        curr->next = temp;
        if (!temp->next) q->rear = temp;
    }
}

job_t dequeue(pqueue_t *q) {
    job_t job = q->front->job;
    node_t *temp = q->front;
    q->front = temp->next;
    if (!q->front) q->rear = NULL;
    free(temp);
    return job;
}

items.title: Implementation 3: Unordered Array
items.text:
#define MAXSIZE 100

struct pqueue {
    job_t jobs[MAXSIZE];
    int count;
};

void enqueue(pqueue_t *q, job_t *job) {
    if (q->count < MAXSIZE)
        q->jobs[q->count++] = *job;
}

job_t dequeue(pqueue_t *q) {
    int max_idx = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < q->count; i++)
        if (q->jobs[i].priority > q->jobs[max_idx].priority)
            max_idx = i;

    job_t job = q->jobs[max_idx];
    // Shift left
    for (int i = max_idx; i < q->count - 1; i++)
        q->jobs[i] = q->jobs[i + 1];
    q->count--;
    return job;
}

items.title: Implementation 4: Ordered Array
items.text:
void enqueue(pqueue_t *q, job_t *job) {
    int i = q->count - 1;
    while (i >= 0 && q->jobs[i].priority >= job->priority) {
        q->jobs[i + 1] = q->jobs[i];
        i--;
    }
    q->jobs[i + 1] = *job;
    q->count++;
}

job_t dequeue(pqueue_t *q) {
    return q->jobs[--q->count];  // Last element = highest priority
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#define MAXSIZE 100

typedef struct {
    int data[MAXSIZE];
    int top;
} Stack;

void init(Stack *s) { s->top = -1; }
int isEmpty(Stack *s) { return s->top == -1; }
int isFull(Stack *s) { return s->top == MAXSIZE - 1; }

void push(Stack *s, int val) {
    if (isFull(s)) return;
    s->data[++s->top] = val;
}

int pop(Stack *s) {
    if (isEmpty(s)) return -1;
    return s->data[s->top--];
}

int peek(Stack *s) {
    if (isEmpty(s)) return -1;
    return s->data[s->top];
}

// 1. Parentheses Matching
int isBalanced(char *expr) {
    Stack s; init(&s);
    for (int i = 0; expr[i]; i++) {
        char ch = expr[i];
        if (ch == '(' || ch == '[' || ch == '{') push(&s, ch);
        else if (ch == ')' || ch == ']' || ch == '}') {
            if (isEmpty(&s)) return 0;
            char top = pop(&s);
            if ((ch == ')' && top != '(') ||
                (ch == ']' && top != '[') ||
                (ch == '}' && top != '{')) return 0;
        }
    }
    return isEmpty(&s);
}

// 2. Infix to Postfix
int prec(char op) {
    if (op == '^') return 3;
    if (op == '*' || op == '/' || op == '%') return 2;
    if (op == '+' || op == '-') return 1;
    return 0;
}

void infixToPostfix(char *infix, char *postfix) {
    Stack s; init(&s);

                postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
            pop(&s);  // Remove '('
        } else {
            while (!isEmpty(&s) && prec(peek(&s)) >= prec(ch))
                postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
            push(&s, ch);
        }
    }
    while (!isEmpty(&s)) postfix[j++] = pop(&s);
    postfix[j] = '\0';
}

// 3. Postfix Evaluation
int evalPostfix(char *postfix) {
    Stack s; init(&s);
    for (int i = 0; postfix[i]; i++) {
        char ch = postfix[i];

            int b = pop(&s);
            int a = pop(&s);
            switch(ch) {

                case '-': push(&s, a - b); break;
                case '*': push(&s, a * b); break;
                case '/': push(&s, a / b); break;

// Helper
Node* create_node(Job j) {
    Node *n = (Node*)malloc(sizeof(Node));
    n->job = j; n->next = NULL;
    return n;
}

// ===== 1. Unordered List =====
void ulist_init(PQList *q) { q->front = q->rear = NULL; }

void ulist_enqueue(PQList *q, Job j) {
    Node *n = create_node(j);
    if (!q->rear) q->front = q->rear = n;
    else { q->rear->next = n; q->rear = n; }
}

Job ulist_dequeue(PQList *q) {
    Node *max_p = NULL, *max_c = q->front, *p = NULL, *c = q->front;
    int max_pri = c->job.priority;
    while (c) {
        if (c->job.priority > max_pri) {
            max_pri = c->job.priority; max_p = p; max_c = c;
        }
        p = c; c = c->next;
    }
    Job job = max_c->job;
    if (!max_p) q->front = max_c->next;
    else max_p->next = max_c->next;
    if (!max_c->next) q->rear = max_p;
    free(max_c);
    return job;
}

// ===== 2. Ordered List =====
void olist_enqueue(PQList *q, Job j) {
    Node *n = create_node(j);
    if (!q->front || q->front->job.priority <= j.priority) {
        n->next = q->front; q->front = n;
        if (!q->rear) q->rear = n;
    } else {
        Node *c = q->front;
        while (c->next && c->next->job.priority > j.priority) c = c->next;
        n->next = c->next; c->next = n;
        if (!n->next) q->rear = n;
    }
}

Job olist_dequeue(PQList *q) {
    Job j = q->front->job;
    Node *t = q->front;
    q->front = t->next;
    if (!q->front) q->rear = NULL;
    free(t);
    return j;
}

// ===== 3. Unordered Array =====
typedef struct { Job jobs[MAXSIZE]; int n; } PQArray;

void uarr_init(PQArray *q) { q->n = 0; }
void uarr_enqueue(PQArray *q, Job j) {
    if (q->n < MAXSIZE) q->jobs[q->n++] = j;
}

Job uarr_dequeue(PQArray *q) {
    int max_i = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < q->n; i++)
        if (q->jobs[i].priority > q->jobs[max_i].priority) max_i = i;
    Job j = q->jobs[max_i];
    for (int i = max_i; i < q->n - 1; i++) q->jobs[i] = q->jobs[i+1];
    q->n--;
    return j;
}

// ===== 4. Ordered Array =====
void oarr_enqueue(PQArray *q, Job j) {
    int i = q->n - 1;
    while (i >= 0 && q->jobs[i].priority >= j.priority) {
        q->jobs[i+1] = q->jobs[i];
        i--;
    }
    q->jobs[i+1] = j; q->n++;
}

Job oarr_dequeue(PQArray *q) {
    return q->jobs[--q->n];
}

    if (!root) {
        node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        n->key = key; n->left = n->right = NULL;
        return n;
    }
    if (key < root->key)
        root->left = insert(root->left, key);
    else
        root->right = insert(root->right, key);
    return root;
}

items.title: Delete (4 Cases)
items.text:
node_t* delete(node_t *root, int key) {
    if (!root) return NULL;

    if (key < root->key)
        root->left = delete(root->left, key);
    else if (key > root->key)
        root->right = delete(root->right, key);
    else {  // Found!
        // Case 1: Leaf
        if (!root->left && !root->right) {
            free(root); return NULL;
        }
        // Case 2: Only right child
        if (!root->left) {
            node_t *t = root->right; free(root); return t;
        }
        // Case 3: Only left child
        if (!root->right) {
            node_t *t = root->left; free(root); return t;
        }
        // Case 4: Two children - use inorder successor
        node_t *succ = root->right;
        while (succ->left) succ = succ->left;
        root->key = succ->key;
        root->right = delete(root->right, succ->key);
    }
    return root;
}

Case 4 Explanation: Replace with inorder successor (smallest in right subtree), then delete that successor.

items.title: Build from Postfix
items.text:
node_t* build_expression_tree(char *postfix) {
    node_t *stack[100];
    int top = -1;

    for (int i = 0; postfix[i]; i++) {
        char ch = postfix[i];
        if (isdigit(ch)) {
            // Operand: create node, push
            node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
            n->key = ch; n->left = n->right = NULL;
            stack[++top] = n;
        } else {
            // Operator: pop 2, create node, push
            node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
            n->key = ch;
            n->right = stack[top--];  // First popped = right
            n->left = stack[top--];   // Second popped = left
            stack[++top] = n;
        }
    }
    return stack[top];  // Root
}

items.title: Evaluate Expression Tree
items.text:
int eval(node_t *root) {
    if (!root->left && !root->right)  // Leaf = operand
        return root->key - '0';

    int left = eval(root->left);
    int right = eval(root->right);

    switch(root->key) {
        case '+': return left + right;
        case '-': return left - right;
        case '*': return left * right;
        case '/': return left / right;
    }
    return 0;
}

items.title: Solution: Threads

  • lthread = 1 → left is thread (not structural)
  • rthread = 1 → right is thread

items.title: Inorder Traversal (Iterative - No Recursion!)

node_t* leftmost(node_t *n) {
    if (!n) return NULL;
    while (n->lthread == 0) n = n->left;  // Follow structural
    return n;
}

void inorder(node_t *root) {
    node_t *curr = leftmost(root);
    while (curr) {
        printf("%d ", curr->key);
        if (curr->rthread == 1)
            curr = curr->right;      // Thread to successor
        else
            curr = leftmost(curr->right);  // Structural right
    }
}

items.title: Definition (Max-Heap)
items.text: Heap = Complete Binary Tree + Parental Dominance 1. Complete: All levels full except last (left-filled) 2. Parental Dominance: Parent ≥ Children (recursively)

items.title: Array Representation (1-indexed)
items.text: Left(i) = 2*i, Right(i) = 2*i+1, Parent(i) = i/2

items.title: Structure
items.text:
#define MAXSIZE 100
struct heap {
    int key[MAXSIZE];
    int n;  // Number of elements
};
typedef struct heap heap_t;

items.title: Heapify (Fix subtree at position i)
items.text:
void heapify(int a[], int n, int i) {
    int largest = i;
    int left = 2*i, right = 2*i + 1;

    if (left <= n && a[left] > a[largest]) largest = left;
    if (right <= n && a[right] > a[largest]) largest = right;

    if (largest != i) {
        swap(&a[i], &a[largest]);
        heapify(a, n, largest);
    }
}

items.title: Build Heap (O(n))
items.text:
void build_heap(heap_t *h, int a[], int n) {
    h->n = n;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) h->key[i] = a[i];
    for (int i = n/2; i >= 1; i--)  // Start from last internal node
        heapify(h->key, h->n, i);
}

items.title: Insert (O(log n))
items.text:
void insert(heap_t *h, int key) {
    int i = ++h->n;
    h->key[i] = key;
    // Bubble up
    while (i > 1 && h->key[i] > h->key[i/2]) {
        swap(&h->key[i], &h->key[i/2]);
        i = i/2;
    }
}

items.title: Delete Max (O(log n))
items.text:
int delete_max(heap_t *h) {
    int max = h->key[1];
    h->key[1] = h->key[h->n--];  // Move last to root
    heapify(h->key, h->n, 1);    // Fix from root
    return max;
}

items.title: Heapsort (O(n log n))
items.text:
void heapsort(int a[], int n) {
    heap_t h; build_heap(&h, a, n);
    for (int i = n; i >= 1; i--)
        a[i] = delete_max(&h);  // Extract max to end
}

// bst_dynamic.c - Complete BST with all operations
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int key;
    struct node *left, *right;
} node_t;

typedef struct { node_t *root; } tree_t;

void init(tree_t *t) { t->root = NULL; }

node_t* create_node(int key) {
    node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    n->key = key; n->left = n->right = NULL;
    return n;
}

// Insert
node_t* insert_rec(node_t *root, node_t *n) {
    if (!root) return n;
    if (root->key > n->key)
        root->left = insert_rec(root->left, n);
    else
        root->right = insert_rec(root->right, n);
    return root;
}

void insert(tree_t *t, int key) {
    t->root = insert_rec(t->root, create_node(key));
}

// Search
node_t* search(node_t *root, int key) {
    if (!root || root->key == key) return root;
    if (key < root->key) return search(root->left, key);
    return search(root->right, key);
}

// Traversals
void inorder(node_t *r) { if (r) { inorder(r->left); printf("%d ", r->key); inorder(r->right); } }
void preorder(node_t *r) { if (r) { printf("%d ", r->key); preorder(r->left); preorder(r->right); } }
void postorder(node_t *r) { if (r) { postorder(r->left); postorder(r->right); printf("%d ", r->key); } }

void display(tree_t *t) {
    printf("Inorder: "); inorder(t->root); printf("\n");
    printf("Preorder: "); preorder(t->root); printf("\n");
    printf("Postorder: "); postorder(t->root); printf("\n");
}

// Delete
node_t* inorder_succ(node_t *r) { while (r->left) r = r->left; return r; }

node_t* delete_rec(node_t *root, int key) {
    if (!root) return NULL;
    if (key < root->key) root->left = delete_rec(root->left, key);
    else if (key > root->key) root->right = delete_rec(root->right, key);
    else {
        if (!root->left && !root->right) { free(root); return NULL; }
        if (!root->left) { node_t *t = root->right; free(root); return t; }
        if (!root->right) { node_t *t = root->left; free(root); return t; }
        node_t *s = inorder_succ(root->right);
        root->key = s->key;
        root->right = delete_rec(root->right, s->key);
    }
    return root;
}

void delete_key(tree_t *t, int key) { t->root = delete_rec(t->root, key); }

// Utilities
int count_nodes(node_t *r) { return r ? 1 + count_nodes(r->left) + count_nodes(r->right) : 0; }
int count_leaves(node_t *r) { 
    if (!r) return 0;
    if (!r->left && !r->right) return 1;
    return count_leaves(r->left) + count_leaves(r->right);
}

node_t* copy_rec(node_t *r) {
    if (!r) return NULL;
    node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    n->key = r->key;
    n->left = copy_rec(r->left);
    n->right = copy_rec(r->right);
    return n;
}

int main() {
    tree_t t1, t2; init(&t1); init(&t2);
    int keys[] = {50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80};
    for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) insert(&t1, keys[i]);

// heap_pq.c - Heap & Priority Queue
#include <stdio.h>
#define MAXSIZE 100

typedef struct {
    int key[MAXSIZE];
    int n;
} heap_t;

void swap(int *a, int *b) { int t = *a; *a = *b; *b = t; }

void heapify(int a[], int n, int i) {
    int largest = i, l = 2*i, r = 2*i+1;
    if (l <= n && a[l] > a[largest]) largest = l;
    if (r <= n && a[r] > a[largest]) largest = r;
    if (largest != i) { swap(&a[i], &a[largest]); heapify(a, n, largest); }
}

void build_heap(heap_t *h, int a[], int n) {
    h->n = n;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) h->key[i] = a[i];
    for (int i = n/2; i >= 1; i--) heapify(h->key, h->n, i);
}

void insert(heap_t *h, int key) {
    int i = ++h->n;
    h->key[i] = key;
    while (i > 1 && h->key[i] > h->key[i/2]) {
        swap(&h->key[i], &h->key[i/2]);
        i = i/2;
    }
}

int delete_max(heap_t *h) {
    int max = h->key[1];
    h->key[1] = h->key[h->n--];
    heapify(h->key, h->n, 1);
    return max;
}

void heapsort(int a[], int n) {
    heap_t h; build_heap(&h, a, n);
    for (int i = n; i >= 1; i--) a[i] = delete_max(&h);
}

typedef struct { heap_t h; } pqueue_t;

void pq_init(pqueue_t *q) { q->h.n = 0; }
void pq_enqueue(pqueue_t *q, int key) { insert(&q->h, key); }
int pq_dequeue(pqueue_t *q) { return delete_max(&q->h); }

int main() {
    printf("=== Heap & Priority Queue Demo ===\n\n");

    // Build heap
    int a[] = {0, 10, 20, 30, 5, 15};  // 1-indexed
    heap_t h; build_heap(&h, a, 5);
    printf("Heap: "); for (int i = 1; i <= h.n; i++) printf("%d ", h.key[i]); printf("\n");

    insert(&h, 25);
    printf("After insert 25: "); for (int i = 1; i <= h.n; i++) printf("%d ", h.key[i]); printf("\n");

    printf("Delete max: %d\n", delete_max(&h));
    printf("After delete: "); for (int i = 1; i <= h.n; i++) printf("%d ", h.key[i]); printf("\n");

    // Heapsort
    int arr[] = {0, 4, 10, 3, 5, 1};
    heapsort(arr, 5);
    printf("Sorted: "); for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) printf("%d ", arr[i]); printf("\n");

    // Priority Queue
    printf("\nPriority Queue:\n");
    pqueue_t pq; pq_init(&pq);
    pq_enqueue(&pq, 10); pq_enqueue(&pq, 30); pq_enqueue(&pq, 20); pq_enqueue(&pq, 5);
    while (pq.h.n) printf("%d ", pq_dequeue(&pq)); printf("\n");

    return 0;
}

items.title: What is Hashing?
items.text: Hashing maps keys to array indices using a hash function. - Goal: O(1) average case for insert, search, delete - Key → Hash Function → Index (0 to TABLESIZE-1)

items.title: Why Hashing?
items.text: Scenario Best Structure Dense integer keys Direct array Sparse integer keys Hash table String keys (identifiers) Hash table Repeated retrieval Hash table Compiler symbol tables Hash table

items.title: Core Concepts
items.text: Term Definition Key Unique identifier for a record Hash Function Maps key → array index Collision Two different keys → same index Overflow Table full, can't insert

items.title: 1. Division Method (Most Common)
items.text:
h(k) = k % TABLESIZE
- TABLESIZE should be prime for better distribution - Simple, fast

int hash_division(int key) {
    return key % TABLESIZE;  // TABLESIZE = 19 (prime)
}

items.title: 2. Multiplication Method
items.text:
h(k) = floor(TABLESIZE * frac(k * A))
- A = constant (e.g., 0.618033... golden ratio) - Works well for non-integer keys

items.title: 3. Mid-Square Method
items.text:
h(k) = middle digits of (k²)
- Example: k=44, 44²=1936, middle=93

items.title: 4. Folding Method (Good for Strings)
items.text:
h(k) = sum of key parts
- Example: 123456 → 12+34+56 = 102

items.title: String Hashing
items.text:
int hash_string(char *s) {
    int sum = 0;
    while (*s) sum += *s++;  // Sum ASCII values
    return sum % TABLESIZE;
}

items.text: Approach Description Pros Cons Open Hashing (Separate Chaining) Linked lists at each index Simple, no overflow, easy delete Extra memory for pointers, cache misses Closed Hashing (Open Addressing) Find next free slot in array Better cache, no pointers Clustering, hard delete, fixed size

items.title: What is a Trie?
items.text: Trie = Tree for storing strings, edges = characters - Not a binary tree - each node can have many children (alphabet size) - Root = empty prefix - Path from root = prefix - is_word_end flag marks complete words

#define ALPHABET_SIZE 256  // Extended ASCII

struct node {
    struct node *child[ALPHABET_SIZE];
    int is_word_end;
};
typedef struct node node_t;

struct trie {
    node_t *root;
};
typedef struct trie trie_t;

items.title: Initialize
items.text:
void init_trie(trie_t *t) {
    t->root = calloc(1, sizeof(node_t));  // calloc zeros all pointers
}

items.title: Insert
items.text:
void insert(trie_t *t, char *word) {
    node_t *curr = t->root;
    for (int i = 0; word[i]; i++) {
        int idx = (unsigned char)word[i];
        if (!curr->child[idx])
            curr->child[idx] = calloc(1, sizeof(node_t));
        curr = curr->child[idx];
    }
    curr->is_word_end = 1;
}

items.title: Search
items.text:
int search(trie_t *t, char *word) {
    node_t *curr = t->root;
    for (int i = 0; word[i]; i++) {
        int idx = (unsigned char)word[i];
        if (!curr->child[idx]) return 0;
        curr = curr->child[idx];
    }
    return curr->is_word_end;
}

items.title: Delete
items.text:
// Returns 1 if node can be freed
int delete_rec(node_t *curr, char *word, int depth) {
    if (!curr) return 0;

    if (word[depth] == '\0') {
        if (!curr->is_word_end) return 0;
        curr->is_word_end = 0;
        // Can delete if no children
        for (int i = 0; i < ALPHABET_SIZE; i++)
            if (curr->child[i]) return 0;
        free(curr);
        return 1;
    }

    int idx = (unsigned char)word[depth];
    if (delete_rec(curr->child[idx], word, depth + 1)) {
        free(curr->child[idx]);
        curr->child[idx] = NULL;
        if (curr->is_word_end) return 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < ALPHABET_SIZE; i++)
            if (curr->child[i]) return 0;
        free(curr);
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

void delete_word(trie_t *t, char *word) {
    delete_rec(t->root, word, 0);
}

items.title: Suffix Trie → Patricia Trie → Suffix Tree
Suffix Trie
items.text:
• Trie of all suffixes of string T
  • Every substring = prefix of some suffix
  • Space: O(n²) - impractical!

items.title: Patricia Trie (Compressed Trie)
items.text:
• Merge "silly nodes" (single child)
  • Chains of single-child nodes → single edge with string label
  • Space: O(n)

items.title: Suffix Tree
items.text:
• Patricia Trie of all suffixes of T$ ($ = unique terminator)
  • Each leaf = starting position of suffix
  • Construction: O(n) with Ukkonen's algorithm
  • Search: O(m) where m = pattern length

items.text:
Suffixes: banana$, anana$, nana$, ana$, na$, a$, $
Compressed → Suffix Tree with edges labeled by string indices

items.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
items.text:
• Single-source shortest path (weighted, non-negative)
  • Uses Min-Heap Priority Queue
  • Time: O((V+E) log V)
void dijkstra(int V, int src) {
    int dist[MAXV];
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) dist[i] = INF;
    dist[src] = 0;

    // Min-heap: (distance, vertex)
    pqueue_t pq; init(&pq);
    enqueue(&pq, src, 0);

    while (!is_empty(&pq)) {
        int u = dequeue_min(&pq);
        for (node_t *p = adj[u]; p; p = p->next) {
            int v = p->vertex, w = p->weight;
            if (dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                enqueue(&pq, v, dist[v]);  // Decrease key
            }
        }
    }
}

items.title: Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree
items.text:
• MST: Connect all vertices with minimum total edge weight
  • Uses Min-Heap Priority Queue
  • Time: O(E log V)
void prim(int V, int start) {
    int key[MAXV], parent[MAXV];
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) { key[i] = INF; parent[i] = -1; }
    key[start] = 0;

    pqueue_t pq; init(&pq);
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) enqueue(&pq, i, key[i]);

    while (!is_empty(&pq)) {
        int u = dequeue_min(&pq);
        for (node_t *p = adj[u]; p; p = p->next) {
            int v = p->vertex, w = p->weight;
            if (in_queue(v) && w < key[v]) {
                key[v] = w; parent[v] = u;
                decrease_key(&pq, v, w);
            }
        }
    }
}

// hash_all_methods.c - Complete Hash Table Implementations
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define TABLESIZE 19
#define WORDSIZE 32

// ==========================================
// 1. SEPARATE CHAINING
// ==========================================
typedef struct node_chain {
    int key;
    char word[WORDSIZE];
    struct node_chain *next;
} NodeChain;

typedef struct { NodeChain *head[TABLESIZE]; } HashChain;

void chain_init(HashChain *h) {
    for (int i = 0; i < TABLESIZE; i++) h->head[i] = NULL;
}

void chain_insert(HashChain *h, int key, char *word) {
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE;
    NodeChain *n = malloc(sizeof(*n));
    n->key = key; strcpy(n->word, word); n->next = h->head[idx];
    h->head[idx] = n;
}

char* chain_search(HashChain *h, int key) {
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE;
    for (NodeChain *p = h->head[idx]; p; p = p->next)
        if (p->key == key) return p->word;
    return "";
}

void chain_display(HashChain *h) {
    for (int i = 0; i < TABLESIZE; i++) {
        printf("%2d: ", i);
        for (NodeChain *p = h->head[i]; p; p = p->next)
            printf("(%d,%s) ", p->key, p->word);
        printf("\n");
    }
}

// ==========================================
// 2. LINEAR PROBING
// ==========================================
typedef struct {
    int in_use;
    int key;
    char word[WORDSIZE];
} NodeLinear;

typedef struct {
    NodeLinear elem[TABLESIZE];
    int count;
} HashLinear;

void linear_init(HashLinear *h) {
    h->count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < TABLESIZE; i++) h->elem[i].in_use = 0;
}

void linear_insert(HashLinear *h, int key, char *word) {
    if (h->count == TABLESIZE) return;
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE;
    while (h->elem[idx].in_use) idx = (idx + 1) % TABLESIZE;
    h->elem[idx].key = key; strcpy(h->elem[idx].word, word);
    h->elem[idx].in_use = 1; h->count++;
}

char* linear_search(HashLinear *h, int key) {
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE, checked = 0;
    while (checked < h->count) {
        if (h->elem[idx].in_use) {
            if (++checked && h->elem[idx].key == key) return h->elem[idx].word;
        }
        idx = (idx + 1) % TABLESIZE;
    }
    return "";
}

// ==========================================
// 3. QUADRATIC PROBING
// ==========================================
typedef struct {
    int in_use;
    int key;
    char word[WORDSIZE];
} NodeQuad;

typedef struct {
    NodeQuad elem[TABLESIZE];
    int count;
} HashQuad;

void quad_insert(HashQuad *h, int key, char *word) {
    if (h->count == TABLESIZE) return;
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE, init = idx, i = 0;
    while (i < TABLESIZE && h->elem[idx].in_use) {
        i++; idx = (init + i*i) % TABLESIZE;
    }
    h->elem[idx].key = key; strcpy(h->elem[idx].word, word);
    h->elem[idx].in_use = 1; h->count++;
}

// ==========================================
// 4. DOUBLE HASHING
// ==========================================
int hash2(int key) { return 7 - key % 7; }

typedef struct {
    int in_use;
    int key;
    char word[WORDSIZE];
} NodeDouble;

typedef struct {
    NodeDouble elem[TABLESIZE];
    int count;
} HashDouble;

void double_insert(HashDouble *h, int key, char *word) {
    if (h->count == TABLESIZE) return;
    int idx = key % TABLESIZE, init = idx, i = 0;
    while (i < TABLESIZE && h->elem[idx].in_use) {
        i++; idx = (init + i * hash2(key)) % TABLESIZE;
    }
    h->elem[idx].key = key; strcpy(h->elem[idx].word, word);
    h->elem[idx].in_use = 1; h->count++;
}

int main() {
    printf("=== Hash Table Comparison ===\n\n");

    // Test data - keys that collide with TABLESIZE=19
    // 40%19=2, 59%19=2, 78%19=2, 97%19=2
    int keys[] = {40, 59, 78, 97, 15, 34, 53};
    char *words[] = {"forty", "fifty-nine", "seventy-eight", "ninety-seven", 
                     "fifteen", "thirty-four", "fifty-three"};
    int n = 7;

    printf("Keys: "); for (int i=0;i<n;i++) printf("%d ", keys[i]); printf("\n");
    printf("Hashes: "); for (int i=0;i<n;i++) printf("%d ", keys[i]%19); printf("\n\n");

    // 1. Separate Chaining
    HashChain hc; 
    chain_init(&hc);
    for (int i=0;i<n;i++) chain_insert(&hc, keys[i], words[i]);
    printf("=== Separate Chaining ===\n");
    chain_display(&hc);

    // 2. Linear Probing
    HashLinear hl; 
    linear_init(&hl);
    for (int i=0;i<n;i++) linear_insert(&hl, keys[i], words[i]);
    printf("\n=== Linear Probing ===\n");
    for (int i=0;i<TABLESIZE;i++)
        if (hl.elem[i].in_use)
            printf("%2d: (%d,%s)\n", i, hl.elem[i].key, hl.elem[i].word);

    // 3. Quadratic Probing
    HashQuad hq = {0};
    for (int i=0;i<n;i++) quad_insert(&hq, keys[i], words[i]);
    printf("\n=== Quadratic Probing ===\n");
    for (int i=0;i<TABLESIZE;i++)
        if (hq.elem[i].in_use)
            printf("%2d: (%d,%s)\n", i, hq.elem[i].key, hq.elem[i].word);

    // 4. Double Hashing
    HashDouble hd = {0};
    for (int i=0;i<n;i++) double_insert(&hd, keys[i], words[i]);
    printf("\n=== Double Hashing ===\n");
    for (int i=0;i<TABLESIZE;i++)
        if (hd.elem[i].in_use)
            printf("%2d: (%d,%s)\n", i, hd.elem[i].key, hd.elem[i].word);

    // Search test
    printf("\nSearch for 78: ");
    printf("Chain:%s Linear:%s Quad:%s Double:%s\n",
           chain_search(&hc, 78), linear_search(&hl, 78),
           "", "");

    return 0;
}

// trie_demo.c - Trie with Autocomplete
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define ALPHABET 256

typedef struct node {
    struct node *child[ALPHABET];
    int is_word_end;
} node_t;

typedef struct { node_t *root; } trie_t;

node_t* create_node() { return calloc(1, sizeof(node_t)); }

void trie_init(trie_t *t) { t->root = create_node(); }

void trie_insert(trie_t *t, char *word) {
    node_t *curr = t->root;
    for (int i = 0; word[i]; i++) {
        int idx = (unsigned char)word[i];
        if (!curr->child[idx]) curr->child[idx] = calloc(1, sizeof(node_t));
        curr = curr->child[idx];
    }
    curr->is_word_end = 1;
}

int trie_search(trie_t *t, char *word) {
    node_t *curr = t->root;
    for (int i = 0; word[i]; i++) {
        int idx = (unsigned char)word[i];
        if (!curr->child[idx]) return 0;
        curr = curr->child[idx];
    }
    return curr->is_word_end;
}

// Display all words from current node
void display_from(node_t *curr, char *prefix, int len) {
    if (curr->is_word_end) {
        prefix[len] = '\0';
        printf("  %s\n", prefix);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < ALPHABET; i++)
        if (curr->child[i]) {
            prefix[len] = (char)i;
            display_from(curr->child[i], prefix, len + 1);
        }
}

void trie_display(trie_t *t) {
    char prefix[100] = {0};
    printf("All words in trie:\n");
    display_from(t->root, prefix, 0);
}

// Autocomplete - find all words with given prefix
void trie_autocomplete(trie_t *t, char *prefix) {
    node_t *curr = t->root;
    for (int i = 0; prefix[i]; i++) {
        int idx = (unsigned char)prefix[i];
        if (!curr->child[idx]) { printf("No words with prefix '%s'\n", prefix); return; }
        curr = curr->child[idx];
    }
    printf("Words with prefix '%s':\n", prefix);
    char full_prefix[100]; strcpy(full_prefix, prefix);
    display_from(curr, full_prefix, strlen(prefix));
}

// Delete word (recursive)
int delete_rec(node_t *curr, char *word, int depth) {
    if (!curr) return 0;
    if (word[depth] == '\0') {
        if (!curr->is_word_end) return 0;
        curr->is_word_end = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < ALPHABET; i++) if (curr->child[i]) return 0;
        free(curr); return 1;
    }
    int idx = (unsigned char)word[depth];
    if (delete_rec(curr->child[idx], word, depth + 1)) {
        free(curr->child[idx]); curr->child[idx] = NULL;
        if (curr->is_word_end) return 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < ALPHABET; i++) if (curr->child[i]) return 0;
        free(curr); return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

void trie_delete(trie_t *t, char *word) { delete_rec(t->root, word, 0); }

int main() {
    trie_t t; trie_init(&t);

    char *words[] = {"cat", "bat", "ball", "rat", "cap", "be", "batman"};
    int n = 7;

    printf("=== Trie Demo ===\n");
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) trie_insert(&t, words[i]);

    printf("\n1. All words:\n"); trie_display(&t);

    printf("\n2. Search 'bat': %d\n", trie_search(&t, "bat"));  // 1
    printf("   Search 'ba': %d\n", trie_search(&t, "ba"));    // 0

    printf("\n3. Autocomplete 'ba':\n"); trie_autocomplete(&t, "ba");
    printf("   Autocomplete 'ca':\n"); trie_autocomplete(&t, "ca");

    printf("\n4. Delete 'bat':\n"); trie_delete(&t, "bat");
    printf("   Search 'bat': %d\n", trie_search(&t, "bat"));  // 0
    printf("   Search 'ball': %d\n", trie_search(&t, "ball")); // 1
    printf("   Autocomplete 'ba':\n"); trie_autocomplete(&t, "ba");

    return 0;
}

// dijkstra_demo.c - Dijkstra's Shortest Path
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <limits.h>
#define MAXV 100
#define INF INT_MAX

typedef struct node {
    int vertex, weight;
    struct node *next;
} node_t;

node_t *adj[MAXV];

// Min-heap for Dijkstra
typedef struct {
    int v[MAXV], dist[MAXV], pos[MAXV];
    int n;
} MinHeap;

void swap_h(MinHeap *h, int i, int j) {
    int tv = h->v[i], td = h->dist[i];
    h->v[i] = h->v[j]; h->dist[i] = h->dist[j]; h->pos[h->v[i]] = i;
    h->v[j] = tv; h->dist[j] = td; h->pos[h->v[j]] = j;
}

void heapify_up(MinHeap *h, int i) {
    while (i > 1 && h->dist[i] < h->dist[i/2]) swap_h(h, i, i/2), i /= 2;
}

void heapify_down(MinHeap *h, int i) {
    int smallest = i, l = 2*i, r = 2*i+1;
    if (l <= h->n && h->dist[l] < h->dist[smallest]) smallest = l;
    if (r <= h->n && h->dist[r] < h->dist[smallest]) smallest = r;
    if (smallest != i) { swap_h(h, i, smallest); heapify_down(h, smallest); }
}

void add_edge(int u, int v, int w) {
    node_t *n = malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    n->vertex = v; n->weight = w; n->next = adj[u]; adj[u] = n;
}

void dijkstra(int V, int src) {
    int dist[MAXV];
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) dist[i] = INF;
    dist[src] = 0;

    MinHeap h = {{0}, {0}, {0}, 0};
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) {
        h.v[++h.n] = i;
        h.dist[h.n] = dist[i];
        h.pos[i] = h.n;
    }
    for (int i = h.n/2; i >= 1; i--) {
        int smallest = i, l = 2*i, r = 2*i+1;
        if (l <= h.n && h.dist[l] < h.dist[smallest]) smallest = l;
        if (r <= h.n && h.dist[r] < h.dist[smallest]) smallest = r;
        if (smallest != i) { swap_h(&h, i, smallest); heapify_down(&h, i); }
    }

    while (h.n > 0) {
        int u = h.v[1];
        int du = h.dist[1];
        h.v[1] = h.v[h.n];
        h.dist[1] = h.dist[h.n];
        h.pos[h.v[1]] = 1;
        h.n--;
        heapify_down(&h, 1);

        if (du == INF) break;

        for (node_t *p = adj[u]; p; p = p->next) {
            int v = p->vertex, w = p->weight;
            if (dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                int idx = h.pos[v];
                h.dist[idx] = dist[v];
                heapify_up(&h, idx);
            }
        }
    }

    printf("Shortest distances from %d:\n", src);
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++)
        printf("  to %d: %d\n", i, dist[i] == INF ? -1 : dist[i]);
}

int main() {
    // Graph with weights
    add_edge(0, 1, 4); add_edge(0, 2, 2);
    add_edge(1, 2, 1); add_edge(1, 3, 5);
    add_edge(2, 3, 8); add_edge(2, 4, 10);
    add_edge(3, 4, 2); add_edge(3, 5, 6);
    add_edge(4, 5, 2);

    printf("=== Dijkstra's Shortest Path ===\n");
    dijkstra(6, 0);

    return 0;
}

items.title: 🎯 What is a Data Structure?
items.text: Definition: A data structure is a scheme of organizing data in the memory of the computer in such a way that various operations can be performed efficiently on this data.

items.title: Why Do We Need Data Structures?
items.text:
1. Large amounts of data - Computers deal with text, images, relational data, etc.
  2. Data is raw material - For information, analytics, business intelligence, advertising
  3. Organization matters - The way data is organized in memory plays a key role in deciding time complexity of algorithms
  4. Data Structures & Algorithms go hand in hand - You can't have efficient algorithms without proper data structures

items.title: Linear Data Structures
items.text:
• Array - Contiguous memory, fixed size
  • Stack - LIFO (Last In First Out)
  • Queue - FIFO (First In First Out)
  • Linked List - Dynamic size, nodes connected by pointers
  • Linear List using Array

items.title: Non-Linear Data Structures
items.text:
• Tree - Hierarchical (Binary Tree, BST, AVL, Heap, Trie)
  • Graph - Network of nodes (vertices) and edges

items.title: 🧠 Abstract Data Type (ADT)
items.text: ADT is used to represent data and operations associated with an entity from the point of view of user irrespective of implementation.

items.title: Key Points:
items.text:
• ADT specifies WHAT operations are supported, not HOW they are implemented
  • Same ADT can be implemented using different data structures
  • Example: Stack ADT can be implemented using Array OR Linked List

items.title: ADT vs Data Structure
items.text: ADT (Interface) Data Structure (Implementation) What operations How operations are implemented Stack: push, pop, peek Array-based Stack Stack: push, pop, peek Linked List-based Stack Queue: enqueue, dequeue Circular Array Queue Queue: enqueue, dequeue Linked List Queue

items.title: Static Memory Allocation
items.text:
• Allocated by compiler at compile time
  • Exact size and type must be known at compile time
  • Memory allocated in stack area
  • Examples: int b; int c[10];

Disadvantages: - Size cannot be altered at runtime - May lead to under/over utilization of memory - Memory cannot be deleted explicitly - Only useful when data size is fixed and known beforehand

items.title: Dynamic Memory Allocation
items.text:
• Memory allocated and released during program execution
  • Operates at low level
  • Functions defined in <stdlib.h>
Function Purpose malloc(size) Allocate memory (uninitialized) calloc(n, size) Allocate memory (zero-initialized) realloc(ptr, new_size) Resize allocated memory free(ptr) Release allocated memory

items.title: malloc()
items.text:
void *malloc(size_t size);
- Takes number of bytes to allocate - Use sizeof to determine size of a type - Returns void* (can be assigned to any pointer) - Returns NULL if no memory available

Example: Allocate space for 100 integers 

int *p;
if ((p = (int*)malloc(100 * sizeof(int))) == NULL) {
    printf("out of memory\n");
    exit(1);
}
// Access as p[0], p[1], ..., p[99] or *p, *(p+1), ...

items.title: calloc()
items.text:
void *calloc(size_t nitem, size_t size);
- Allocates memory and initializes to zero - Requires two arguments: number of items and size of each item

Example: 

int *p = (int*)calloc(100, sizeof(int)); // 100 ints, all zeros

items.title: realloc()
items.text:
void *realloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size);
- Resizes previously allocated block - Two arguments: pointer to existing block, new size

Example: 

int *ip = (int*)malloc(100 * sizeof(int));
// ... later need twice as much ...
ip = (int*)realloc(ip, 200 * sizeof(int));

items.title: free()
items.text:
void free(void *ptr);
- Deallocates memory allocated by malloc/calloc/realloc - Takes a pointer as argument

Critical Concepts: - Dangling Pointer: Pointer to memory that has been freed - Memory Leak: Allocated memory with no pointer to it (cannot be freed)

// DANGEROUS - Dangling pointer
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
free(p);
// p now dangles - points to freed memory!
// *p = 10; // UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR!

// DANGEROUS - Memory leak
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
*p = 30;
p = malloc(sizeof(int)); // First block lost forever!

items.title: Dangling Pointer Prevention
items.text:
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
*p = 100;
free(p);
p = NULL;  // ALWAYS set to NULL after free!

items.title: Memory Leak Prevention
items.text:
// BAD - Memory leak
int *leak = malloc(sizeof(int));
leak = malloc(sizeof(int));  // First block lost!

// GOOD - Free before reassign
int *good = malloc(sizeof(int));
*good = 42;
free(good);  // Free first!
good = malloc(sizeof(int));
*good = 84;
free(good);

Memory Leak Lost allocated memory - ALWAYS FREE!

// memory_demo.c - Dynamic Memory Allocation Demo
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int main() {
    printf("=== Dynamic Memory Demo ===\n\n");

    // 1. malloc
    printf("1. malloc():\n");
    int *p = (int*)malloc(5 * sizeof(int));
    if (!p) { printf("Failed\n"); return 1; }
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) p[i] = (i+1)*10;
    printf("Allocated 5 ints: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) printf("%d ", p[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(p);
    p = NULL;  // Good practice: set to NULL after free

    // 2. calloc (zero-initialized)
    printf("\n2. calloc():\n");
    int *q = (int*)calloc(5, sizeof(int));
    printf("Zero-initialized: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) printf("%d ", q[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(q);

    // 3. realloc
    printf("\n3. realloc():\n");
    int *r = (int*)malloc(3 * sizeof(int));
    r[0] = 1; r[1] = 2; r[2] = 3;
    printf("Before realloc: ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) printf("%d ", r[i]);
    r = (int*)realloc(r, 6 * sizeof(int));
    r[3] = 4; r[4] = 5; r[5] = 6;
    printf("\nAfter realloc:  ");
    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) printf("%d ", r[i]);
    printf("\n");
    free(r);

    // 4. Structure allocation
    printf("\n4. Structure allocation:\n");
    struct student {
        char name[20];
        int roll;
        float marks;
    };
    struct student *s = (struct student*)malloc(sizeof(struct student));
    strcpy(s->name, "Alice");
    s->roll = 101;
    s->marks = 95.5;
    printf("Student: %s, Roll: %d, Marks: %.1f\n", s->name, s->roll, s->marks);
    free(s);

    printf("\n=== Dangling Pointer Demo ===\n");
    int *dang = (int*)malloc(sizeof(int));
    *dang = 100;
    printf("Before free: *dang = %d\n", *dang);
    free(dang);
    // dang is now DANGLING - don't use it!
    dang = NULL;  // Always set to NULL after free

    printf("\n=== Memory Leak Demo ===\n");
    // BAD: memory leak
    // int *leak = malloc(sizeof(int));
    // leak = malloc(sizeof(int));  // First block lost!

    // GOOD: free before reassign
    int *good = malloc(sizeof(int));
    *good = 42;
    free(good);
    good = malloc(sizeof(int));
    *good = 84;
    free(good);
    printf("No leaks!\n");

    return 0;
}

What is a Linked List?
items.text: A linked list is a linear data structure where: - Elements (nodes) are NOT stored in contiguous memory - Each node contains data and a pointer (link) to the next node - Head/start pointer points to the first node - Last node's link contains NULL

        │       │       │

       10      20      30

items.title: 📋 Node Structure
items.text:
struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *link;
};
typedef struct node NODE;

items.title: Structure Breakdown:
items.text:
• data - The actual value stored (can be any type)
  • link - Pointer to the next node (self-referential structure)
  • NODE - Typedef for cleaner code

void insert_at_pos(NODE **head, int value, int pos) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    temp->data = value;
    temp->link = NULL;

    if (*head == NULL || pos == 1) {
        // Empty list or insert at front
        temp->link = *head;
        *head = temp;
        return;
    }

    NODE *curr = *head;
    NODE *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;

    // Traverse to position
    while (curr != NULL && i < pos) {
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->link;
        i++;
    }

    if (curr == NULL) {
        // Position beyond end - insert at end
        prev->link = temp;
    } else {
        // Insert between prev and curr
        prev->link = temp;
        temp->link = curr;
    }
}

#include <stdlib.h>

    int data;
    struct node *next;
} NODE;

NODE *create_node(int data) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    if (!temp) { printf("Memory full\n"); exit(1); }
    temp->data = data;
    temp->next = NULL;
    return temp;
}

void insert_front(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    temp->next = *head;
    *head = temp;
}

void insert_end(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    if (*head == NULL) { *head = temp; return; }
    NODE *curr = *head;
    while (curr->next) curr = curr->next;
    curr->next = temp;
}

void insert_at_pos(NODE **head, int data, int pos) {
    if (pos <= 1 || *head == NULL) { insert_front(head, data); return; }
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;
    while (curr && i < pos) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; i++; }
    if (!curr) { prev->next = temp; }
    else { prev->next = temp; temp->next = curr; }
}

void display(NODE *head) {
    printf("List: ");
    while (head) { printf("%d → ", head->data); head = head->next; }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

    insert_end(&head, 20);
    insert_end(&head, 30);

    insert_front(&head, 5);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 20 → 30

    insert_at_pos(&head, 15, 3);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 15 → 20 → 30

    insert_at_pos(&head, 100, 10);  // Beyond end
    display(head);  // ... → 100

    return 0;
}

// dll_complete.c - Doubly Linked List
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *prev;
    struct node *next;
} NODE;

typedef struct {
    NODE *head, *tail;
} dll_t;

void init_dll(dll_t *list) { list->head = list->tail = NULL; }

NODE* create_node(int data) {
    NODE *n = malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    n->data = data; n->prev = n->next = NULL;
    return n;
}

void insert_front(dll_t *list, int data) {
    NODE *n = create_node(data);
    n->next = list->head;
    if (!list->head) list->head = list->tail = n;
    else { list->head->prev = n; list->head = n; }
}

void insert_end(dll_t *list, int data) {
    NODE *n = create_node(data);
    n->prev = list->tail;
    if (!list->tail) list->head = list->tail = n;
    else { list->tail->next = n; list->tail = n; }
}

void delete_node(dll_t *list, NODE *n) {
    if (!n) return;
    if (n == list->head && n == list->tail) list->head = list->tail = NULL;
    else if (n == list->head) { list->head = n->next; list->head->prev = NULL; }
    else if (n == list->tail) { list->tail = n->prev; list->tail->next = NULL; }
    else { n->prev->next = n->next; n->next->prev = n->prev; }
    free(n);
}

void display_forward(dll_t *list) {
    NODE *c = list->head;
    printf("Forward: ");
    while (c) { printf("%d ", c->data); c = c->next; }
    printf("\n");
}

void display_backward(dll_t *list) {
    NODE *c = list->tail;
    printf("Backward: ");
    while (c) { printf("%d ", c->data); c = c->prev; }
    printf("\n");
}

int main() {
    dll_t list; init_dll(&list);

    insert_end(&list, 10);
    insert_end(&list, 20);
    insert_end(&list, 30);
    insert_front(&list, 5);

    display_forward(&list);   // 5 10 20 30
    display_backward(&list);  // 30 20 10 5

    return 0;
}

items.text:
• Last node points back to first node
  • Forms a cycle
  • Head pointer can point to ANY node in the cycle
  • No NULL termination - use do-while for traversal

items.title: Why do-while?
items.text:
• While loop would not execute if we check condition first
  • do-while executes at least once, then checks
  • Guarantees we visit all nodes exactly once

items.title: Problem Statement:
items.text: n people stand in a circle. Starting from a designated person, count k people and eliminate the k-th person. Continue until one survivor remains.

items.title: Algorithm:
items.text:
1. Create circular list with people 1 to n
  2. Count k-1 steps
  3. Remove k-th person
  4. Repeat until one remains

items.title: Implementation:
items.text:
int josephus(int n, int k) {
    // Create circular list 1..n
    node_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        temp->key = i; temp->next = NULL;
        if (!head) head = tail = temp;
        else { tail->next = temp; tail = temp; }
    }
    tail->next = head;  // Make circular

    node_t *curr = head, *prev = tail;

    while (curr->next != curr) {
        // Count k-1 steps
        for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) {
            prev = curr;
            curr = curr->next;
        }
        // Eliminate curr
        prev->next = curr->next;
        free(curr);
        curr = prev->next;
    }
    int survivor = curr->key;
    free(curr);
    return survivor;
}

// sll_complete.c - Complete Singly Linked List Implementation
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *next;
} NODE;

NODE *create_node(int data) {
    NODE *temp = (NODE*)malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    if (!temp) { printf("Memory full\n"); exit(1); }
    temp->data = data;
    temp->next = NULL;
    return temp;
}

void insert_front(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    temp->next = *head;
    *head = temp;
}

void insert_end(NODE **head, int data) {
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    if (*head == NULL) { *head = temp; return; }
    NODE *curr = *head;
    while (curr->next) curr = curr->next;
    curr->next = temp;
}

void insert_at_pos(NODE **head, int data, int pos) {
    if (pos <= 1 || *head == NULL) { insert_front(head, data); return; }
    NODE *temp = create_node(data);
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;
    while (curr && i < pos) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; i++; }
    if (!curr) { prev->next = temp; }
    else { prev->next = temp; temp->next = curr; }
}

void delete_front(NODE **head) {
    if (!*head) return;
    NODE *temp = *head;
    *head = (*head)->next;
    free(temp);
}

void delete_end(NODE **head) {
    if (!*head) return;
    if (!(*head)->next) { free(*head); *head = NULL; return; }
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    while (curr->next) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; }
    prev->next = NULL;
    free(curr);
}

void delete_at_pos(NODE **head, int pos) {
    if (!*head) return;
    if (pos <= 1) { delete_front(head); return; }
    NODE *curr = *head, *prev = NULL;
    int i = 1;
    while (curr && i < pos) { prev = curr; curr = curr->next; i++; }
    if (!curr) { printf("Invalid position\n"); return; }
    prev->next = curr->next;
    free(curr);
}

void display(NODE *head) {
    printf("List: ");
    while (head) { printf("%d → ", head->data); head = head->next; }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

int main() {
    NODE *head = NULL;

    printf("=== Singly Linked List Demo ===\n");
    insert_end(&head, 10);
    insert_end(&head, 20);
    insert_end(&head, 30);
    display(head);  // 10 → 20 → 30

    insert_front(&head, 5);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 20 → 30

    insert_at_pos(&head, 15, 3);
    display(head);  // 5 → 10 → 15 → 20 → 30

    delete_front(&head);
    display(head);  // 10 → 15 → 20 → 30

    delete_end(&head);
    display(head);  // 10 → 15 → 20

    delete_at_pos(&head, 2);
    display(head);  // 10 → 20

    return 0;
}

// circular_josephus.c - Circular List & Josephus Problem
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int key;
    struct node *next;
} node_t;

node_t* create_node(int key) {
    node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
    temp->key = key;
    temp->next = NULL;
    return temp;
}

void insert_clist(node_t **head, int key) {
    node_t *temp = create_node(key);
    if (*head == NULL) {
        temp->next = temp;
        *head = temp;
    } else {
        temp->next = (*head)->next;
        (*head)->next = temp;
    }
}

void disp_clist(node_t *head) {
    if (!head) { printf("Empty\n"); return; }
    node_t *temp = head;
    printf("Circular: ");
    do {
        printf("%d ", temp->key);
        temp = temp->next;
    } while (temp != head);
    printf("\n");
}

// Josephus Problem
int josephus(int n, int k) {
    node_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        node_t *temp = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        temp->key = i; temp->next = NULL;
        if (!head) head = tail = (node_t*)malloc(sizeof(node_t));
        else { tail->next = temp; tail = temp; }
    }
    tail->next = head;  // Make circular

    node_t *curr = head, *prev = head;
    // Find tail (node before head)
    while (prev->next != head) prev = prev->next;

    while (curr->next != curr) {
        for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) {
            prev = curr;
            curr = curr->next;
        }
        prev->next = curr->next;
        free(curr);
        curr = prev->next;
    }
    int survivor = curr->key;
    free(curr);
    return survivor;
}

int main() {
    printf("=== Circular List Demo ===\n");
    node_t *head = NULL;
    for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) insert_clist(&head, i*10);
    printf("List: "); disp_clist(head);

    printf("\n=== Josephus Problem ===\n");
    printf("n=7, k=3: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(7, 3));  // 4
    printf("n=5, k=2: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(5, 2));  // 3
    printf("n=41, k=3: Survivor = %d\n", josephus(41, 3)); // Historical: 31

    return 0;
}

// dll_complete.c - Doubly Linked List
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct node {
    int data;
    struct node *prev;
    struct node *next;
} NODE;

typedef struct {
    NODE *head, *tail;
} dll_t;

void init_dll(dll_t *list) { list->head = list->tail = NULL; }

NODE* create_node(int data) {
    NODE *n = malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    n->data = data; n->prev = n->next = NULL;
    return n;
}

void insert_front(dll_t *list, int data) {
    NODE *n = malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    n->data = data; n->prev = NULL; n->next = list->head;
    if (!list->head) list->head = list->tail = n;
    else { list->head->prev = n; list->head = n; }
}

void insert_end(dll_t *list, int data) {
    NODE *n = malloc(sizeof(NODE));
    n->data = data; n->next = NULL; n->prev = list->tail;
    if (!list->tail) list->head = list->tail = n;
    else { list->tail->next = n; list->tail = n; }
}

void delete_node(dll_t *list, NODE *n) {
    if (!n) return;
    if (n == list->head && n == list->tail) list->head = list->tail = NULL;
    else if (n == list->head) { list->head = n->next; list->head->prev = NULL; }
    else if (n == list->tail) { list->tail = n->prev; list->tail->next = NULL; }
    else { n->prev->next = n->next; n->next->prev = n->prev; }
    free(n);
}

void display_forward(dll_t *list) {
    NODE *c = list->head;
    printf("Forward: ");
    while (c) { printf("%d ", c->data); c = c->next; }
    printf("\n");
}

void display_backward(dll_t *list) {
    NODE *c = list->tail;
    printf("Backward: ");
    while (c) { printf("%d ", c->data); c = c->prev; }
    printf("\n");
}

int main() {
    dll_t list; init_dll(&list);

    insert_end(&list, 10);
    insert_end(&list, 20);
    insert_end(&list, 30);
    insert_front(&list, 5);

    display_forward(&list);   // 5 10 20 30
    display_backward(&list);  // 30 20 10 5

    return 0;
}
